title: Nutrient Composition of Maize Legume, Silages Fortified with Dicalcium Phosphate and Molasses
content: Integrating legumes into maize silage systems may improve forage yield, nutritive value, and fermentation quality, but responses vary with legume species, harvest stage, and additive use. This study evaluated the effects of soybean, cowpea, and pigeon pea inclusion, harvest stage, and silage additives on biomass yield, proximate composition, microbial quality, and fermentation characteristics of maize-legume silages. Maize was intercropped with each legume and harvested at 4, 8, and 12 weeks after planting. Silages were prepared from sole maize and maize-legume mixtures and treated with dicalcium phosphate (DCP), molasses, or their combination. Pigeon pea mixtures produced the highest fresh biomass yield at 4 weeks (28.35 kg/6.25 m²), whereas cowpea mixtures recorded the highest dry matter yield at 12 weeks (9.13 kg). Crude protein was highest in pigeon pea and soybean mixtures receiving DCP plus molasses (20.32% and 19.22%, respectively). Soybean-based silages showed relatively stable pH values (5.40–5.56), while overall fermentation pH ranged from 5.30 to 5.90 and temperature from 27.2 to 28.5 °C. Molasses improved moisture retention and fat content but was associated with increased yeast and mould counts in pigeon pea silage. Overall, legume inclusion improved nutritive characteristics, with responses dependent on legume species, harvest stage, and additive combination.
